title: Hazard-portfolio patterns in US food recall severity reveal transferable pathogen signals and firm-specific compliance signals
task: Identify structural determinants of US food recall severity via machine learning and conditional mutual information
key_results: Hazard-portfolio-dominated firm-level patterns (hazard mediates 27–63% of firm–severity association, firm-intrinsic residual ≥37%); pathogen signals (Salmonella, Listeria) universally associated with Class I (92% accuracy across unseen firms), compliance signals firm-specific; event-disjoint cross-validation F1=0.609 (XGBoost) vs. 0.406 (firm-history baseline)
comments: Nuanced analysis separates universal from firm-specific signals; event-disjoint evaluation is rigorous unit-of-analysis; caveat: SKU-level pseudoreplication inflates metrics reported in prior food-safety ML literature.

model_io.model: XGBoost multi-class classifier + conditional mutual information
inputs: FDA enforcement records (28,448 records, 2012–2025): hazard, product, firm, announcement entity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Firm-level severity patterns are driven by hazard-product portfolio rather than firm-intrinsic compliance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; hazard mediates 27–63% of association; firm residual ≥37% under all specifications

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pathogen contamination signals generalize across firms; compliance signals do not
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; pathogen Class I accuracy 92% on unseen firms; compliance signals fail to transfer

title: Explainable ensemble learning using SHAP for ERP anomaly detection
task: ERP anomaly detection via explainable ensemble learning with SHAP attribution
key_results: Six-model ensemble achieves F1=0.8437 (95% CI [0.8305, 0.8569]) on 41,933 held-out procurement transactions vs. top individual models (GB 0.9321, Robust AE 0.9254); 0.49% cross-validation CV vs. 1.4–2.1% for individual models; 19.4% relative FPR reduction; Pareto-front analysis confirms 63 non-trivial subsets; deployed value: $4.1M fraud prevention, net $3.27M benefit (conservative ROI 392%)
comments: Ensemble trades peak accuracy for stability and explainability (regulatory requirement); three-layer interpretability stack (feature importance, decision rules 87.3% coverage, SHAP) enables audit compliance; cross-industry generalization confirmed (F1 range [0.794, 0.862]); optimistic ROI scenario (884%) speculative, not empirically validated.

model_io.model: Six-model weighted ensemble (Isolation Forest, LOF, OC-SVM, Elliptic Envelope, GB, Robust AE)
SHAP explainer

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ensemble improves stability and interpretability vs. best individual model without prohibitive accuracy loss
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; F1 ensemble 0.8437 (vs. top individual 0.9321) trades 8.4 pp accuracy for 3.2× lower CV and regulatory compliance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ensemble generalizes across heterogeneous ERP scenarios
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; cross-scenario F1 range [0.794, 0.862]

title: Named entity recognition for coal mining machine assembly based on domain large language model
task: Named entity recognition for coal mining machine assembly via domain-specific fine-tuned LLM
key_results: QLoRA fine-tuning achieves BLEU-4 0.6580 (vs. 0.0612 baseline), F1-score 0.893 on assembly NER task; reduces computational resource demands
comments: Domain adaptation via QLoRA is efficient; F1-score of 0.893 is solid but baseline (generic BERT) comparison unclear; qualitative error analysis missing.

model_io.model: QLoRA fine-tuned domain-specific LLM
outputs: named entity recognition (entity spans and labels)

hypotheses.hypothesis: QLoRA fine-tuning on domain-specific data improves NER performance for coal mining assembly vs. off-the-shelf LLM
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; BLEU-4 and F1-score improvements substantial

title: Digital twin–driven multiscale modelling for real-time defect prediction in metal additive manufacturing
task: Real-time defect prediction in metal additive manufacturing via digital twin and multiscale modeling
key_results: 98.72% mean defect-detection rate, 11.3 ms inference latency on edge; 34.6% reduction in scrap rate, 41.2% reduction in predictive maintenance lead time; CNN-LSTM achieves macro-averaged F1=0.9841 on six defect classes
comments: Hierarchical PINN surrogates enable real-time inference, but framework complexity (25 governing equations) may limit adoption; validation limited to NIST AM-Bench datasets (IN625, Ti-6Al-4V).

model_io.model: Hierarchical physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogates
CNN-LSTM spatio-temporal defect classifier
outputs: six defect classes (porosity, lack-of-fusion, cracking, balling, keyholing, delamination)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multiscale coupling via hierarchical PINNs improves real-time defect detection vs. offline simulations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; porosity and cracking prediction improved vs. offline baseline

title: Parasitically coupled 16-port massive MIMO antenna for mmWave applications
task: Design compact 16-port massive MIMO antenna for mmWave 5G/6G communications
key_results: Compact antenna (26.2×79×0.508 mm³) resonating at 40 GHz with 40 dB peak return loss; gain 17.9 dB at 39 GHz, 17.2 dB at 41 GHz; SAR 0.045 W/kg at 40 GHz
comments: Excellent antenna metrics across 3GPP bands n259, n260, n262; equivalent circuit validation in ADS adds rigor, but multi-port MIMO isolation metrics not detailed.

model_io.model: 16-port parasitically coupled massive MIMO antenna on modified ground plane
outputs: SAR on human male hand model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Parasitic element coupling with defected ground enables compact 16-port performance in mmWave band
hypotheses.result: High gain (17.9–17.2 dB) and SAR compliance (0.045 W/kg) achieved across licensed 5G bands

title: Metamaterial-enhanced MIMO antenna array system for non-invasive cerebral hemorrhage assessment in elderly and disabled patients
task: Design metamaterial-enhanced MIMO antenna for non-invasive microwave brain imaging
key_results: UWB MIMO antenna (3.1–6 GHz) with envelope correlation coefficient <0.005, diversity gain >9.9 dB, mutual coupling below −15 dB; enables portable stroke detection
comments: Clinically motivated design with strong electromagnetic metrics; human head integration is simulated but real-world imaging validation against CT/MRI gold standard is not demonstrated.

model_io.model: T-shaped two-port MIMO antenna on FR4 (εr=4.3) integrated with human head model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Low mutual coupling and high diversity enable effective microwave imaging for hemorrhage detection
hypotheses.result: Mutual coupling <−15 dB, ECC <0.005 achieved; potential for detecting scattering parameter changes from hemorrhage confirmed

title: Design of a slotted bowtie dual-polarized antenna for Sub-6 GHz multi-service wireless applications
task: Design dual-band dual-polarized antenna for sub-6 GHz wireless communications
key_results: Operating frequencies 2.52 GHz and 4.42 GHz with port isolation >30 dB; antenna gain improved from 2 dBi to 7.14 dBi with reflector integration
comments: Practical engineering design with strong experimental validation; reflector placement at 28.4 mm is empirically optimized but lacks theoretical justification for generalization.

model_io.model: Slotted bowtie MIMO antenna on FR4 substrate
outputs: gain measurements at 2.52 GHz and 4.42 GHz

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reflector placement enhances gain and improves dual-band performance
hypotheses.result: Gain increased to 7.14 dBi average; dual-band operation confirmed

title: Accurate alpha-particle stopping power measurements in graphenic carbon foils and their application to high-precision, non-destructive areal density determination
task: Determine areal density of thin graphenic carbon foils via alpha-particle energy loss spectroscopy
key_results: Non-destructive areal density measurement with <1% relative uncertainty; fitted mean excitation energies Iadj=(73±2) eV (KETEK) and (85±3) eV (Applied Nanotech); stopping-power model uncertainties dominated by foil mass/area/composition metrology
comments: Precision nuclear method with careful uncertainty budgeting; model-dependent interpretation of compositional differences between foils limits applicability; thin-target approximation restricts scope.

model_io.model: Alpha-particle stopping-power measurement in graphenic carbon foils
inputs: GC foil samples with known nominal areal density

hypotheses.hypothesis: Modified Bethe formalism with Barkas/Bloch corrections and empirically adjusted Iadj describes stopping power across 5.0–5.8 MeV range
hypotheses.result: Fitted Iadj values (73±2 eV and 85±3 eV) consistent with foil composition and microstructure differences
